what: argenx develops antibody medicines for rare autoimmune diseases. Its product Vyvgart treats generalised myasthenia gravis and is being extended into other conditions where the immune system attacks the body.
customers: Health systems and insurers, with medicines prescribed by neurologists and specialists.
money: intravenous and subcutaneous treatment for myasthenia gravis and CIDP
moat: A validated antibody-fragment approach to removing harmful antibodies, with clinical data in a disease where few alternatives exist, and patent protection into the next decade.
risks: Almost all revenue comes from one medicine
Competitors are developing drugs with the same mechanism
Reimbursement decisions in Europe can delay launches
The shares price in continued rapid expansion into new diseases
opportunities: Revenue grew about 89% in the last financial year
Each new approved indication opens another patient population
It holds about $5.2 billion of cash against almost no debt
watch: Vyvgart sales growth and trial results in new autoimmune indications.
